title: DNA Extraction Protocol for Eastern Banjo Frog Using Gentra Puregene Tissue Kit
author: Qiye Li
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcy6ixze

steps.title: Mince frozen liver tissue
steps.instruction: Using a scalpel blade on ice, mince approximately 30 mg of frozen liver tissue.

steps.title: Lyse tissue with Cell Lysis solution
steps.instruction: Perform cell lysis and protein digestion.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 900 µl Cell Lysis Solution into a 1.5 ml microfuge tube.
Add the minced tissue to the tube.
Add 6 µl Proteinase K solution (20 mg ml⁻¹).
Mix by inverting the tube 25 times.
Incubate at 55 °C overnight with agitation.

steps.title: Treat lysate with RNase A
steps.instruction: Add RNase A to the lysate and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Heat RNase A solution (12 mg ml⁻¹) to 100 °C for 10 min.
Add 1.5 µl of the heated RNase A to the lysate tube.
Mix by inverting the tube 25 times.
Incubate at 37 °C for 60 min.
Cool the tube to room temperature.
Add 300 µl Protein Precipitation Solution.
Vortex vigorously at high speed for 20 seconds.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 16 000 × g.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Recover DNA by isopropanol precipitation and spooling.

substeps.instruction: Add 900 µl cold 100 % isopropanol to a clean 2 ml microfuge tube.
Carefully pour the supernatant from the previous step into the tube.
Gently invert the tube 50 times to mix.
Spool the precipitated DNA onto a sterile glass rod.

steps.title: Wash spooled DNA
steps.instruction: Clean the spooled DNA with ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Immerse the spooled DNA in 300 µl 70 % ethanol.
Transfer the DNA to a clean microfuge tube containing 500 µl 70 % ethanol.
Store the tube at –20 °C for 2 h.

steps.title: Dry and elute DNA
steps.instruction: Dry the DNA and dissolve it in elution buffer.

substeps.instruction: Dry the DNA at room temperature for 1 h by inverting the glass rod.
Dissolve the DNA in 200 µl of the recommended elution buffer (add more buffer if DNA does not fully dissolve).
